issues.description: The template file src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java declares a class named AnimalFarm instead of the expected Farm class described in the problem statement and used in Main.java. This class-name mismatch prevents students from compiling Main.java (which expects Farm) and from following the UML/design that requires a Farm class.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename and implement the class in template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java to public class Farm (not AnimalFarm) and ensure its public API (constructors and methods) matches the UML and the Main.java usage. This will align the template with the problem specification and the solution.

issues.description: The template Farm.java file contains duplicated/embedded code (a second package declaration and a nested duplicate class definition inside a method) which creates syntax errors and makes the file uncompileable. For example, there is a 'package de.tum.cit.ase;' and another 'public class AnimalFarm {' inserted inside the singFarmSong method body. This malformed structure will block students from compiling or starting the exercise.
issues.suggestedFix: Replace the contents of template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java with a single well-formed public class Farm implementation (or a clean skeleton) that matches the UML: no nested package declarations, no duplicate class definitions, and properly placed methods (including singFarmSong and singFarmSongVerse). Use the solution repository Farm.java as a reference for structure and placement of methods.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML describe a class named 'Farm', but the template repository's Farm.java declares a public class 'AnimalFarm'. This inconsistent identifier for the same conceptual entity (the farm class) breaks the direct mapping students must make from the assignment description to the starter code and will likely cause compilation confusion since the file is named Farm.java but the public class differs.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the public class in the template from 'AnimalFarm' to 'Farm' and ensure the class implementation matches the UML and required methods/attributes. This aligns the template with the problem statement and the solution implementation and avoids compilation/name-mismatch issues.
